name: Low-Poly Diorama
summary: A toy-like autumn miniature world of flat-shaded triangle facets in soft afternoon light, with tilt-shift blur at the screen edges.
description: Every character, prop, pickup and ground tile is a real triangle mesh, projected with a fixed 44° three-quarter orthographic camera and flat-shaded by one warm sun plus a cool-sky / warm-ground ambient. Meshes are pre-rendered into sprite canvases (16 yaw angles x a few animation frames), so it reads as 3D but costs like 2D. The ground is a jittered triangle lattice lit from a tiny height field, giving the signature faceted meadow. Soft indigo cast shadows, glowing carved faces and a tilt-shift band at the top and bottom make it feel like a photographed tabletop diorama.
avoidFor: games needing hundreds of unique animated models

difficulty.why: Describing triangle meshes through coordinates is fiddlier than voxels, but it becomes predictable once you are used to it.

technique.renderer: Canvas 2D (procedural, no image assets) with a tiny software 3D pipeline: mesh -> yaw -> orthographic 3/4 projection -> flat shading -> painter's sort -> baked sprites
technique.resolution: Native resolution. Sprites are baked at K = clamp(round(screenHeight/360 * 4)/4, 2, 4) px per world unit (2.5 px/unit at a 900 px tall screen); the ground is baked in 256-unit chunks at up to 3 px/unit (groundResMax 3).
technique.summary: Real triangle meshes built from lathes, boxes, icospheres and folded leaf blades, flat-shaded per face with a fixed sun and pre-rendered into sprite sheets at 16 yaw angles; the ground is a lit, jittered triangle lattice.
technique.linework: No outlines. Each facet is filled and then stroked in its own colour (lineWidth 0.85 sprite px, 0.6 for decals, 0.5 for gems, round joins) only to hide anti-aliasing seams. Silhouettes read through value contrast against the ground, never through ink lines.
technique.shading: Flat per-face Lambert: colour * (SKY*h + GND*(1-h) + SUN*max(0, n.L)) with h = 0.5 + 0.5*nz, SKY [0.47,0.52,0.67], GND [0.52,0.44,0.38], SUN [0.7,0.62,0.45]. Volume comes from facet orientation plus alternating rib colours and ±3-7 % per-face colour jitter. Emissive faces (carved eyes, windows, cracks) skip lighting.
technique.lighting: One warm sun from upper-left-front, L = normalize(-0.58, 0.3, 0.76) (x right, y towards camera, z up). Additive warm radial glows ('lighter') around glowing faces, lanterns and gems. Cast shadows are the mesh projected along the sun, blurred and tinted indigo #2c3263 (props: #7d86c4, multiplied at 62 %).
technique.texture: None on surfaces. Texture comes from geometry: 24-unit jittered ground triangles with 4 colour variants per biome, low-amplitude macro tint, and baked micro-props (grass tufts, flowers, pebbles, fallen leaves).

palette.name: Meadow
palette.role: Grass ground base (variants #95b16f #a3bd7d #99b572), ~55 % of the screen

palette.name: Pumpkin
palette.role: Hero head, pumpkin props – main warm accent

palette.name: Carved Glow
palette.role: Emissive carved faces, lantern glow (hot core #fff1a6, rim #6e2e10)

palette.name: Cape Blue
palette.role: Hero cape – the only cool saturated mid-tone on the hero

palette.name: Turnip Lilac
palette.role: Main enemy colour (top half of turnips)

palette.name: Ember Crack
palette.role: Emissive cracks and core on the brute (core #ffe58c, body #7f5c95)

palette.name: Mint Gem
palette.role: Small XP gem; big gem uses #5cbdf6

palette.name: Shadow Indigo
palette.role: Actor cast shadows and AO blobs (never black)

paletteRules: Everything is mid-value and slightly desaturated; the only fully saturated colours are emissive (carved glow, cracks, gems).
The ground stays in a narrow value band (grass #95b16f-#a3bd7d) so actors pop through hue: orange hero, lilac enemies, white ghosts.
Shadows and vignettes are cool indigo/violet (#2c3263, rgba(60,55,100,.22), rgba(70,62,110,.26)), never pure black or grey.
Each material has exactly 2-4 base colours (e.g. pumpkin #f48a2c / #e27526) – the lighting creates the rest of the ramp.
Autumn tree crowns come from 4 warm triads: oranges #ee8b3a/#e47a31/#f2a046, reds #dc5d43/#cf4d3c/#e6714b, yellows #ecb544/#e3a23c/#f2c35a, rusts #d07a3f/#e09447/#c4653a.
No pure white surfaces except hit flashes and sparkle stars; no pure black anywhere (darkest is #161b33 inside ghost eyes).

typography.role: Headings, HUD numbers, damage numbers, level-up title
typography.css: font: 800 58px/1 'Baloo 2', 'Nunito', system-ui, sans-serif; color: #fff; letter-spacing: 1px; text-shadow: 0 1px 0 #f39a52, 0 2px 0 #ee8c45, 0 3px 0 #e8803c, 0 4px 0 #e07434, 0 5px 0 #d6692e, 0 12px 20px rgba(60,40,100,.45);

background.summary: An endless faceted tabletop: a jittered equilateral triangle lattice (cell 24 world units) whose vertices carry a biome id and a tiny height; each triangle is flat-shaded from its height-field normal with the same sun as the models. Biomes (grass, autumn forest, sand, rock, ploughed field, farm yard) blend with jagged triangle borders; decals and prop shadows are baked into 256-unit chunks.
layers: Triangle lattice: CS = 24, row height 24*0.866, vertex jitter ±26 % x / ±23 % y, odd rows offset half a cell
Per-facet colour: one of 4 biome variants by hash, 40 % of mixed-biome border facets mixed 50 % with the neighbour; macro tint from fbm at 1/520 scale (±6 %)
Per-facet flat shading from the vertex height field (biome base height + roughness * noise + 6 * perlin(x/280))
Field biome: furrow ridges every 14 units (north face darker, south face lighter) with tiny two-tone vine triangles
Decals on an 11-unit jittered grid: grass tufts, 5-petal flowers, pebbles, mushrooms, mini pumpkins (baked low-poly sprites) and two-tone fallen leaf triangles
Prop shadows baked into the chunk with 'multiply' at alpha 0.62, colour #7d86c4

characters.summary: Chunky toy figures, 1.1x scaled, ~17 units wide and ~31 tall, built from lathes (8-16 segments), boxes and 20-face icospheres. The hero is a big pumpkin head (radius 7.8, 60 % of the height) on a small body with linen shirt, red scarf, blue half-cape, brown pants and boots. Faces are carved flat polygons projected onto the head's front (+x) as three stacked emissive layers. Pre-rendered at 16 yaw angles x 6 walk frames + 1 idle frame.
rules: Head-to-body ratio about 1:1 – the head is the silhouette; keep it the largest and most saturated shape.
Every actor has a glowing or high-contrast face on the +x (front) side so facing reads at 16 directions.
Use 5-9 lathe segments for bodies, 16 for the hero head; never smooth – faceting is the style.
Colour each ring/segment explicitly (rib alternation, top/bottom split) instead of texturing.
Animate by rebuilding the mesh per frame (leg swing ±0.62 rad, arm swing ±0.7 rad, bob 0.35) and baking; never squash the sprite except on death.
Enemies must differ by hue and silhouette: lilac/cream turnip (round + leaf crown), pale blue ghost (tapered trailing sheet), purple rock brute (3x size, orange cracks).

effects.name: Faceted shards
effects.how: Hits and deaths spray tiny flat triangles (size 1.7-4.2 units) with gravity 260 and drag 1.6; colour comes from an 8-step brightness palette of the victim's colours, chosen per frame by |cos(rotation)| so shards flicker like spinning facets.

effects.name: Low-poly puffs
effects.how: Dash, spawn and death dust are baked jittered icospheres (r 3, sub 1) in cream #f6eedf, pale blue #e0ecfb, sand #d8c09a or #fff3c9, scaled up 0.7->1.4 while fading.

effects.name: Spawn ring
effects.how: A dark ground ellipse (alpha 0.5) plus a cream ellipse stroke (#f6ecd6) expanding to 2x radius with 6 puffs around it; the enemy sprite is revealed bottom-up by clipping its height with outQuad.

effects.name: Hit flash
effects.how: A white silhouette copy of the current sprite (source-in fill #ffffff) drawn on top at alpha = flash * 1.1.

effects.name: Carved glow
effects.how: An additive ('lighter') radial sprite (rgba 255,225,140,.9 -> 255,150,50,0, r 10 units) drawn over the face, alpha 0.22 ± 0.06 flicker at 9 rad/s, only when the face points toward the camera.

effects.name: Seed projectile
effects.how: A flattened lathe seed (#f8ebc6 / rim #dfc58c) pre-rendered in 8 roll frames, rotated to its direction, with a tapered cream trail triangle (#fff6dc, alpha .45, up to 16 units) and a dark ground dot.

effects.name: Gem pickup
effects.how: 8-face octahedron (mint #4fe3b0 or sky #5cbdf6) spinning through 8 frames over a quarter turn, with a soft radial halo, bobbing 2.2 ± 0.8 units above a small shadow dot.

effects.name: Level-up
effects.how: A gold ellipse ring #ffd666 expanding 8->52 units, a warm additive glow and 14 rising 4-point star motes alternating #ffe27a and #bdf5df.

ui.summary: Soft, rounded, toy-like HUD: cream pill panels (#fffaf2) with a violet drop shadow and a subtle inset bottom lip, thick cream borders around pill bars with glossy gradient fills and a white highlight stripe. Text in Baloo 2 800, ink #3e3a58. Icons are the same low-poly meshes rendered into round radial-gradient badges.

motion: Hero: 6 walk frames per stride cycle (frame = floor(anim*0.5*6) % 6) plus 1 idle frame; vertical hop |sin(2π*anim*0.5)| * 1.1 units; idle breathing bob 0.35 ± 0.35 at 2.4 rad/s.
Small enemy: 4 frames, cycle rate anim*0.55, hop 1.4 units; brute: 4 frames at anim*0.42, hop 0.6; ghost: 4 frames at 1.4 cycles/s, hovering 2.5 ± 1.6 units, alpha 0.8.
Facing is a smoothed yaw (angleLerp, rate 0.22 hero, 0.16 enemies, 0.08 brute) quantised to 16 baked angles.
Death: 0.22 s – sprite stretches 1.3x wide, 0.45x tall while fading, white flash overlay at 55 %.
Gems spin 1.5 quarter-turns per second; lanterns hover 9 ± 1.2 units at 4 rad/s; damage numbers pop 0.55 -> 1.15 scale in the first 14 % of their life.
Hurt invulnerability blinks at 18 Hz between alpha 0.5 and 1.
do: Build every visible thing as a real triangle mesh and flat-shade it with the same sun vector and ambient constants.
Pre-render meshes into sprites at 16 yaw angles and a handful of animation frames; draw sprites, not meshes, per frame.
Keep facets large and visible – 5-9 segment lathes, icospheres with subdivision 0 or 1, ±10-15 % vertex jitter on organic shapes.
Use emissive (unlit) polygons for faces, windows and cracks, stacked dark-rim / fill / hot-core with negative depth bias.
Ground every object with a sun-projected, blurred indigo shadow plus an AO blob.
Finish with the tilt-shift bands (top 20 % hazy-light, bottom 17 % violet) and a soft side vignette.
Pick colours as 2-4 base tones per material and let the lighting make the ramp.
dont: Don't add black outlines or cel ink – the look depends on outline-free facets.
Don't use smooth gradients or Gouraud/Phong shading on models; one colour per triangle.
Don't use textures, photos or noise grain on surfaces.
Don't render meshes live every frame for crowds – it will not hold 60 fps with hundreds of enemies.
Don't make shadows grey or black, and don't drop them – floating sprites break the diorama illusion.
Don't mix camera pitches or light directions between assets; every sprite must share pitch 44° and the same sun.
Don't saturate the ground; bright grass kills the contrast with orange/lilac actors.
performance: All meshes are baked once at init (about 16 yaws x 7 hero frames, 16 x 4 per enemy type, props, decals, icons) – that is the main load cost (a few hundred ms). Per frame only drawImage blits, a few additive glows and particles are drawn, so hundreds of enemies are cheap. Ground chunks (256 units) are built incrementally with a generator over several frames; prop shadows are baked into them. The tilt-shift costs two 1/8-scale band copies per frame. Shadow blur uses ctx.filter at bake time only.
